title: Lake Mega-Chad
summary: Lake Mega-Chad was the largest pluvial lake in Africa, about 360,000 km2 at its peak in the southern Sahara. A 2015 PNAS study dated its highstand from about 11,500 to 5,000 years ago, with levels falling rapidly around 5,000 years ago; its northern Bodélé basin finally dried out around 1,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: ka values used as stated, with no 1950 or 2000 offset. Humid conditions began around 15 ka; levels fell rapidly around 5 ka; the Bodélé basin dried finally around 1 ka (Armitage et al. 2015). ScienceDaily puts the peak around 6,000 years ago.

when.display: Highstand c. 11,500 to 5,000 years ago (peak around 6,000 years ago)

where.modern_name: Lake Chad basin (proxy pin at the modern Lake Chad), on the borders of Nigeria, Chad, Cameroon and Niger
where.historical_name: Palaeolake Mega-Chad in the southern Sahara, before any states

importance.justification: The largest lake of the African humid period; its collapse exposed the Bodélé dust source.

sources.title: West African monsoon dynamics inferred from abrupt fluctuations of Lake Mega-Chad
